παρεν-θήκη , ἡ,
A.something put in beside, addition, τοιήνδε . . παρενθήκην ἐποιήσατο, of works undertaken in completion of others, Hdt. 1.186 ; παρενθήκην ἔχρησε ἐς Μιλησίους delivered an oracle by way of parenthesis, Id. 6.19 ; τοῦ λόγου π. ποιεέσκετο τήνδε, ὡς . . Id. 7.5 , cf. 171 ; ἑτέρας τοῦ πολέμου π. ἐποιεῖτο undertook other business in the intervals of the war, Plu. Pomp. 41 ; π. ὄψου,
= παροψώνημα , Poll. 6.56 ; of a remedy interposed in a difficult situation,
Lib. Or. 59.95 .
II. smaller wares taken as an addition to the cargo, opp. ἡ ἐμπορία, Plu. 2.151e , cf. Poll. 1.99 , Hsch.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
